history.why: rescaled: the number is an index with a ceiling of 100, not a percentage

encode allocations fall 62% (68.6M -> 26.3M): a fold's accumulator now proves unique, so appends extend the builder instead of allocating a header each time. The +5 emitted lines are #322's wrapper inlining, which is what made the mutate path reachable at all.

a string's header and bytes are one allocation, not two: decode allocations 12,924,473 -> 11,353,217 and encode 26,327,708 -> 22,130,027. The +5 emitted lines are still #322's wrapper inlining, which bought the encode cut above.

a record's fields live after its header, not in a second allocation: encode allocations 22,130,027 -> 18,785,627. Field count is fixed at construction and set writes through the existing slots, so there is nothing to grow.

put extends a unique map in place: decode allocations 11,353,217 -> 10,518,917 and a map literal counts as a unique source. The +10 emitted lines are the put_mut declare (5 samples) plus the wrapper-inlining lines already priced.

unused runtime declares no longer ride into every program: emitted lines 1,903 -> 1,488, 27% below the original baseline. This is the fix for the twice-flagged emitted-lines regression, downward rather than re-priced.

byte-builder growth is malloc-backed and a mut-grow frees its predecessor: encode arena blocks 905 -> 684, the doubling trail pays for one buffer at a time. Prerequisite for the beat license on bytes-crossing loops.

the three encode loops rewind: a bytes accumulator crossing by pointer identity is licensed, sorted views join builder buffers outside the arena, and the registry sweep retires. Encode arena blocks 905 -> 5; kq peak 116.1 -> 77.3 mb.
string literals build once into permanent slots: encode allocations 18,774,865 -> 16,274,462. The +56 emitted lines are one slot global per interned literal, priced against a 2.5M-allocation cut.

dead buffers from proven-unique growth go to a size-classed shelf and the next collection reuses them: decode allocations 10,518,914 -> 8,941,967 with 452,550 reuses on the decode board. Rewinds flush the shelf so no entry outlives its region.
put growth donates through its mut path and grow caps land on shelf classes: decode allocations 8,941,967 -> 8,341,217 with 516,750 reuses, and kq's decode peak drops below jq's.
baseline established at the utf-8 short-ascii fast path
the full stack composed: shelf reuse plus literal interning together read 8,341,214 decode and 16,259,944 encode allocations.
lambda-head beta step in inference narrows sets; encode arena flattens 5 to 4 blocks (one more loop licensed to beat)

the model gains a one-shot peak-footprint term at runtime weight: the looping gauntlet's rewinds hide the decode garbage cohort freeing exists to reclaim, and peak is the scoreboard row still lost; paid by trimming both alloc terms, both block terms, and compile_rounds — block counts cede most because peak bytes measure what they proxied

structured cohort freeing: a qualified call from user code with immutable args marks the arena, and the pop evacuates the result through the carry machinery and rewinds the construction garbage when a half-megabyte grew; the round-trip one-shot peak falls 9.4 to 6.3 MB for a 32k-alloc evacuation copy, the trade the peak term was added to price
std/json strings on the bytes builder: decode allocs -9%, alloc bytes -32%, arena peak down a block

transient builders grow in the arena: decode true peak 24.4M->3.1M (the leak the RSS showed at 25MB), oneshot pays one arena block, +3 IR lines per sample for the signed-cap fast path; model sums arena+builder peak and gains the decode peak term at 0.10

zerocopy chunks registered at handoff, freed by the frame's rewind: encodebench true peak 113M->4.6M (RSS 85->6.2MB); encode peak term joins at 0.06 so the workload's peak is priced like the other two

the basket enters: three programs and a compile sampled too narrow a shelf, and a 20x string build and a 200x sort both left the number untouched. runtime weight redistributed proportionally (0.721 unchanged in total, 0.15 of it to the basket); compile split untouched. new terms enter at ratio one, so this move is the re-weighting alone.

skipping over a cursor is index arithmetic: list/drop walked and discarded one element at a time, costing a step record and an advanced cursor each. basket allocations 91,864 -> 79,952, and the merge sort pays it too (sort_shape 33,403 -> 29,470).

a fold's reducer writes in place: the emitter now resolves marks inside a lifted lambda, and the analysis only makes them where it can account for when the lambda runs. to_list 4,015 -> 15, basket 79,952 -> 74,380, sort_shape 29,470 -> 24,401.

a conditional folder writes in place too: fusion turns a select into 'if (p v) (push a v) a', and every path there either writes on the accumulator or hands it back. to_list over a select 4,015 -> 15, basket 74,369 -> 71,364, peak 69.2 MB -> 68.2 MB.

taking from a cursor is a window: capped over a cursor rebuilt an advanced cursor, a step, a fresh cap and another step every element, and a bounded window carries position and limit in one record. take 12,019 -> 6,020, basket 71,364 -> 66,432, sort_shape 24,401 -> 20,468 (merging halves takes).

the sort slices its halves instead of walking them: msort materialised each half through take/drop, paying adapter records per element per level, where builtin_slice copies the range once. sort 20,468 -> 3,509 at 500 elements and 28,010 at 4,000, basket 66,432 -> 49,473.

the sort's halves are index ranges, not lists: splitting by take and drop walked each half element by element at every level to build a list read once and thrown away. sort 500 23,486 -> 2,512, sort 4,000 -> 20,014, sort_shape 20,468 -> 2,513, basket 66,432 -> 48,477.

a builtin forces its arguments, so a sibling may read the accumulator: tally is fold coll {:} (m x -> put m x (bump m[x])), which mentions the map twice and holds it once. Without the discount the fold copied its map every element. tally 12,024 -> 25 allocations and 128,000 -> 0 map-header bytes, fused_tally 1,590 -> 94, basket 48,477 -> 36,478.

a repeated pure interpolation is evaluated once: reading a key then writing it builds the key twice as written, and the licence is narrow — an interpolation over names, numbers and arithmetic only, never inside a lambda. repeated 14,759 -> 7,388, basket 36,478 -> 29,107, growing_map 3,207 -> 1,616, readwrite_map 611 -> 311.

a record whose fields are all read by one constructor is finished when it runs, so the new record goes in its storage. The judgment is local — every caller hands the parameter over, and every mention in the arm is inside that one expression — so the shared fixpoint is untouched. record updates 4,005 -> 3, basket 29,107 -> 25,105.

a cap around a cursor is walked by index: pulling a window through next built a step and a fresh window every element, both read once and dropped. take 3,000 of 4,000 went 6,023 allocations -> 20, sum over a take 6,017 -> 14, basket 25,105 -> 24,102.

a string built by joining onto itself writes into one buffer: the seed is converted where it enters the group from outside, so its header predates the loop's marks and survives every rewind, and the join only ever writes into that header. basket string build 4,004 allocations -> 9, 100,000 appends 162 ms -> 10.3 ms, basket 24,102 -> 20,107.

a library no longer emits an entry stub calling an entry it does not have: the compiler stopped claiming the name `main`, so a file with definitions and no `pub play` is compiled as the library it always was. emitted lines fall five per sample.
inference visits only what a change can reach: 6223 to 4448 on the module sample, with every emitted line identical

the score is four terms now — memory and performance, compiling and running — not twelve counters; the ten points are the model changing, not the compiler improving, and compile memory enters at its own baseline

compile speed reads lib/json now, not five fixtures whose 126 visits no compiler change can move; the 0.14 is that term giving up an improvement banked on a sample too small to mean anything, not the front end getting slower
the survivor region absorbs the repair: kq's copy walk is linear again, and encode allocs fall 3,984 with carry_dedup 6800 -> 68

a growing list of scalars carries: the gate refused it because copying a growing accumulator every rewind was quadratic, and k_buf_perm took its storage out of the arena so there is nothing left to copy. basket peak 5,242,896 -> 2,097,152 for eighteen allocations, ch10 counters a quarter of the arena at 100,000 and byte-identical below that
